arxiv-1602-07212.title: Singular Instantons and Painlevé VI
arxiv-1602-07212.creator: Richard MUÑIZ MANASLISKI
arxiv-1602-07212.description: Abstract We consider a two parameter family of instantons, which is studied in [Sadun L., Comm. Math. Phys. 163 (1994), 257–291], invariant under the irreducible action of SU 2 \operatorname{SU}_{2} on S 4 S^{4} , but which are not globally defined.

arxiv-1805-01952.title: A Coherent Unsupervised Model for Toponym Resolution 4 Conference: The 2018 Web Conference; April 23–27, 2018; Lyon, France WWW 2018: The 2018 Web Conference, April 23–27, 2018, Lyon, France DOI: 10.1145/3178876.3186027 ISBN: 978-1-4503-5639-8/18/04 CCS: Information systems Location based services C
arxiv-1805-01952.creator: Ehsan Kamalloo, Davood Rafiei
arxiv-1805-01952.description: Abstract . Toponym Resolution, the task of assigning a location mention in a document to a geographic referent (i.e., latitude/longitude), plays a pivotal role in analyzing location-aware content. However, the ambiguities of natural language and a huge number of possible interpretations for toponyms constitute insurmountable hurdles for this task.

arxiv-2202-10114.title: Path regularity of Brownian motion and Brownian sheet
arxiv-2202-10114.creator: H. Kempka, C. Schneider, and J. Vybiral
arxiv-2202-10114.description: Abstract By the work of P. Lévy, the sample paths of the Brownian motion are known to satisfy a certain Hölder regularity condition almost surely. This was later improved by Ciesielski, who studied the regularity of these paths in Besov and Besov-Orlicz spaces.

arxiv-2206-14796.title: On the Robustness of Dialogue History Representation in Conversational Question Answering: A Comprehensive Study and a New Prompt-based Method
arxiv-2206-14796.creator: Zorik Gekhman, Nadav Oved, Orgad Keller, Idan Szpektor, Roi Reichart
arxiv-2206-14796.description: Abstract Most works on modeling the conversation history in Conversational Question Answering (CQA) report a single main result on a common CQA benchmark. While existing models show impressive results on CQA leaderboards, it remains unclear whether they are robust to shifts in setting (sometimes to more realistic ones), training data size (e.g. from large to small sets) and domain.

arxiv-2403-12942.title: The physics of Core-Collapse Supernovae: explosion mechanism and explosive nucleosynthesis
arxiv-2403-12942.creator: Luca Boccioli *, Lorenzo Roberti *
arxiv-2403-12942.description: Abstract Recent developments in multi-dimensional simulations of core-collapse supernovae have considerably improved our understanding of this complex phenomenon. In addition to that, one-dimensional (1D) studies have been employed to study the explosion mechanism and its causal connection to the pre-collapse structure of the star, as well as to explore the vast parameter space of supernovae.

arxiv-2410-14104.title: Accelerating operator Sinkhorn iteration with overrelaxation
arxiv-2410-14104.creator: Tasuku Soma, André Uschmajew
arxiv-2410-14104.description: Abstract We propose accelerated versions of the operator Sinkhorn iteration for operator scaling using successive overrelaxation. We analyze the local convergence rates of these accelerated methods via linearization, which allows to determine the asymptotically optimal relaxation parameter based on Young’s SOR theorem.

arxiv-2412-09733.title: Geometric transport signatures of strained multi-Weyl semimetals
arxiv-2412-09733.creator: Varsha Subramanyan, Shi-Zeng Lin, Avadh Saxena
arxiv-2412-09733.description: Abstract The minimal coupling of strain to Dirac and Weyl semimetals, and its modeling as a pseudo-gauge field has been extensively studied, resulting in several proposed topological transport signatures. In this work, we study the effects of strain on higher winding number Weyl semimetals and show that strain is not a pseudo-gauge field for any winding number larger than one.

arxiv-2503-05363.title: Lonely passengers: a short proof
arxiv-2503-05363.creator: John Haslegrave
arxiv-2503-05363.description: Abstract A fixed number of passengers independently board one of several buses uniformly at random. The lonely passenger problem is to prove that the probability of at least one passenger being the only one in their bus is increasing in the number of buses.

arxiv-2510-16666.title: Closed Neighborhood Balanced k k -Coloring of Graphs
arxiv-2510-16666.description: Abstract For a simple graph G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) and a positive integer k ≥ 2 k\geq 2 , a coloring of vertices of G G using exactly k k colors such that every vertex has an equal number of vertices of each color in its closed neighborhood is called closed neighborhood-balanced k k -coloring ,

arxiv-2511-10588.title: Probing jet hadrochemistry modification with measurements of π \mathbf{\pi} , K, and p in jets and the underlying event in pp and Pb–Pb collisions at s NN = 5.02 \mathbf{\sqrt{\textit{s}_{\textup{NN}}}=5.02} TeV
arxiv-2511-10588.creator: \firstname Sierra \lastname Cantway for the ALICE Collaboration
arxiv-2511-10588.description: Abstract Measurements of jet substructure observables in heavy-ion (HI) collisions provide powerful constraints on the microscopic mechanisms of interactions between energetic partons and the quark–gluon plasma (QGP). Although there has been remarkable progress in measuring inclusive jet substructure, a complete understanding of identified particle production inside jets (jet hadrochemistry) and its modification in HI collisions remains elusive.

pmc-10574689.title: Methanol Extracts from Cirsium japonicum DC. var. australe Kitam. and Their Active Components Reduce Intracellular Oxidative Stress in Caenorhabditis elegans
pmc-10574689.creator: Pei-Ling Yen, Ting-An Lin, Wei Lin Chuah, Chih-Yi Chang, Yen-Hsueh Tseng, Chia-Yin Huang, Jeng-Chuann Yang, Fu-Lan Hsu, Vivian Hsiu-Chuan Liao, Pyrzyńska Krystyna, Aleksandra Sentkowska, Violeta Ivanova-Petropulos
pmc-10574689.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Cirsium japonicum DC. has been used as an herbal remedy and often involves using the whole plant or roots. However, the bioactivities of different parts of the plant have been far less explored. This study aimed to evaluate the antioxidative ability of methanol extracts from the flowers, leaves, stems, and roots of the Cirsium plant and their possible active components against juglone-induced oxidative stress in the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans.

pmc-11198509.title: Medical Therapies to Improve Left Ventricular Outflow Obstruction and Diastolic Function in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
pmc-11198509.creator: Mason Zhu, Klevin Roger L Reyes, Gizem Bilgili, Robert J Siegel, Brian Lee Claggett, Timothy C Wong, Ahmad Masri, Srihari S Naidu, Andrew Willeford, Florian Rader
pmc-11198509.description: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy—both obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM) and nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (nHCM) subtypes—is the most common monogenic cardiomyopathy. Its structural hallmarks are abnormal thickening of the myocardium and hyperdynamic contractility, while its hemodynamic consequences are left ventricular outflow tract or intracavitary obstruction (in oHCM) and diastolic dysfunction (in both oHCM and nHCM).

pmc-11504401.title: Oral Spore-Based Probiotic Supplementation Alters Post-Prandial Expression of mRNA Associated with Gastrointestinal Health
pmc-11504401.creator: Brian K McFarlin, Sarah E Deemer, Elizabeth A Bridgeman, Marie Černá
pmc-11504401.description: Background/Objectives: Unregulated post-prandial dietary endotoxemia may accumulate over time and underlie the development of chronic disease (e.g., leaky gut, inflammatory bowel disease, etc.), for which oral probiotic supplementation may be a prophylactic. The purpose of this study was to determine if 45 d of oral spore-based probiotic supplementation altered gastrointestinal-associated mRNA expression following a high-fat meal.

pmc-11638836.title: Investigation of the effects of Periplaneta americana (L.) extract on ischemic stroke based on combined multi-omics of gut microbiota
pmc-11638836.creator: Xin Yang, Canhui Hong, Tangfei Guan, ChengGui Zhang, Peiyun Xiao, Yongshou Yang, Huai Xiao, Zhengchun He
pmc-11638836.description: Ischemic stroke (IS) is a highly lethal type of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease. Improving survival rates and promoting recovery in patients with IS pose significant challenges, however, recent research has identified the gut–brain axis as a therapeutic target. In this study, we evaluated the regulatory effect of Periplaneta americana (L.

pmc-12537798.title: Impact of Wearing Defocus Incorporated Multiple Segments Spectacle Lenses for 12 Months on Accommodation and Binocular Functions in Myopic Children
pmc-12537798.creator: Fatin Nur Najwa Norazman, Bariah Mohd-Ali, Syarifah Faiza Syed Mohd Dardin, Mizhanim Mohamad Shahimin, Norliza Mohamad Fadzil, Mohd Norhafizun Mohd Saman
pmc-12537798.description: IntroductionSpectacle lens design for myopia control incorporates either lenslet or diffusion technology to slow down the eye growth, which may impact the binocular vision functions of a myopic child. This study aimed to investigate the changes in accommodation and binocular functions in myopic children over 12 months wear of myopia control spectacle lenses.

pmc-12706482.title: Anastomotic pseudoaneurysm presenting 50 years after common carotid artery–subclavian artery bypass: illustrative case
pmc-12706482.creator: Mayuko Otomo, Tomoo Inoue, Nobuo Noshita, Toshie Takahashi, Jun Kikuchi, Hidenori Endo
pmc-12706482.description: BACKGROUNDCommon carotid artery (CCA)–subclavian artery bypass is performed for CCA occlusive disease. Reported complications include infection, occlusion, anastomotic leakage, and nerve injury. A pseudoaneurysm at the anastomotic site is rare, and most develop within 1–2 years after the procedure. The authors present a case of an anastomotic pseudoaneurysm occurring 50 years after bypass surgery.

pmc-13072669.title: Tumor cell death by ferroptosis contributes to an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment in syngeneic murine models of cancer
pmc-13072669.creator: Nneka E. Mbah, Damien Sutton, Hanna S. Hong, Rashi Singhal, Rosa E. Menjivar, Matthew D. Perricone, Heather Giza, Peter Sajjakulnukit, Amy L. Myers, Zeribe C. Nwosu, Jonathan M. Alektiar, Jason Lin, Daniel Long, Anthony C. Andren, Li Zhang, Howard C. Crawford, Timothy L. Frankel, Marina Pasca di Mag
pmc-13072669.description: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by profound metabolic rewiring and a strongly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, both of which contribute to poor therapeutic responses. Immunogenic cell death (ICD) represents a potential strategy to overcome immune suppression by coupling tumor cell death to anti-tumor immune activation.

pmc-13392073.title: Observation of quantum information collapse-and-revival in a strongly-interacting Rydberg atom array
pmc-13392073.creator: De-Sheng Xiang, Yao-Wen Zhang, Hao-Xiang Liu, Peng Zhou, Dong Yuan, Kuan Zhang, Shun-Yao Zhang, Biao Xu, Lu Liu, Yitong Li, Lin Li
pmc-13392073.description: Interactions of isolated quantum many-body systems typically scramble local information into the entire system and make it unrecoverable. Ergodicity-breaking systems possess the potential to exhibit fundamentally different information scrambling dynamics beyond this paradigm. For many-body localized systems with strong ergodicity breaking, local transport vanishes and information scrambles logarithmically slowly.

pmc-13481164.title: The impact of flexible human resource management on employees’ workplace well-being based on self-determination theory
pmc-13481164.creator: Yixin Zhang, Mengli Liu, Tianyu Du, Weipeng Lin, Xiaohui Qu, Bing Liu
pmc-13481164.description: IntroductionFlexible human resource management (FHRM) has become an effective means for enhancing an organization’s adaptability and responsiveness through the efficient acquisition and optimal deployment of human resources. Although previous studies argued that FHRM can positively influence organizational and individual overt behavioral outcomes, some overlooked its impact on the well-being of employees.

pmc-13537830.title: Clinical evaluation of the CrossNN DNA methylation classifier for central nervous system tumors
pmc-13537830.creator: Jonas Dahnoun, Léon C. van Kempen, Senada Koljenović, Ken Op de Beeck, Tomas Menovsky, Bart Feyen, Melek Ahmed, Anne Sieben, Karen Zwaenepoel
pmc-13537830.description: DNA methylation profiling is an integral diagnostic tool in the classification of central nervous system (CNS) tumors. While the Heidelberg CNS Tumor Methylation Classifier is widely used to support CNS tumor diagnostics, new classifiers such as CrossNN are emerging. However, their clinical performance and added value within routine diagnostic workflows remain insufficiently explored.
